title: Belt Driven Plug Fan Parts
description: FanPedia's exploded view of an Arrangement 9P belt driven plug fan (p. 14) with ten numbered markers, leader lines and a label column. Explore mode previews each part's name and description; quiz mode hides the labels and describes each part by its job, with two attempts, a hint after the first miss and mastery at 8 of 10 on the first attempt.

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
educational.topic: Parts of an Arrangement 9P belt driven plug fan
learningObjectives: The learner will identify the ten labeled parts of an Arrangement 9P belt driven plug fan on an exploded view, given each part's function.

accessibility.notes: The drawing is a labelled SVG group; every numbered marker is a focusable role=button and Tab walks them in number order; Enter or Space selects one; focus or hover previews its name and description. During the quiz the markers are named only 'Part n' until resolved, labels and leader lines are hidden, and hints never name the answer. Verdicts and prompts are announced through FP.announce (aria-live). ✓/✗ glyphs, solid/dashed borders and an 'Answer' badge pair with colour. Text is 12 px or larger; markers keep a constant pixel size; the label column moves below the drawing on narrow screens.

simulation.modelType: labeled diagram with locate quiz (FP.Overlay callout engine on FP.CalloutQuiz)
rules: Explore mode: hover or focus previews a part's name and description; click, Enter or Space opens it and counts it as visited; never scored.
Quiz mode: 10 prompts in a seeded shuffle (the same order for every learner; Start over reshuffles).
Two attempts per prompt; the first wrong answer shows a hint that does not name the answer; the second reveals the answer and counts as missed.
Selecting empty space uses no attempt.
Only first-attempt answers count toward mastery; mastery is 8 of 10.
assumptions: FanPedia p. 14 exploded view, with the printed labels, leader lines and the 'Arr. 9P Fan' tag removed; marker positions are percentages of the image.
limitations: The drawing is FanPedia's, not a specific current catalog model; the drawing shows two sheaves and two bearings, each pair with one marker.

sources: FanPedia p. 14 (Exploded Views: Plug Fans, Belt Driven Plug Fans, Arr. 9P fan): drawing and part names

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore labelled markers on the real FanPedia drawing first, then retrieval practice: find each part from a description of its job, with a hint after the first miss and immediate correction.
keyQuestions: Which parts end up inside the plenum, which in the wall, and which outside the process airstream?
Which part fills the wall opening so the plenum keeps its insulating value?
commonMisconceptions: The mounting panel and the insulation plug are the same part.
A plug fan's motor and belts sit inside the plenum with the impeller.
The mounting panel always holds up the fan.
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt score shown as 'First-attempt score: n of 10'; mastery is 8 of 10 on the first attempt.
